summary: Iter 106: Tested new public endpoint GET /api/merchant/qr/share-page and the mobile-viewport browser render of that share page. Backend 4/5 pytest (public share-page endpoint): valid code + channel=whatsapp returns 200 text/html with 'no-store' in Cache-Control, contains navigator.share, 'Share on WhatsApp', inline with data:image/png;base64 poster, and the caption text incl. https link; channel=system swaps button label to 'Share poster + message'; invalid code=BADCODE returns 404; link without ref= is transparently rebuilt server-side and still returns 200. **1 FAIL — Real XSS/serialisation bug**: caption containing '' is emitted verbatim inside the CAP JS string literal (json.dumps does NOT escape ' block. Browser mobile-viewport render (420x800) of the share-page URL: poster renders, caption bubble shows message with https link rendered as , #go button 'Share on WhatsApp' visible; clicking #go (headless — no navigator.canShare) triggers the fallback download of the poster PNG and navigates to https://wa.me/?text= (browser followed 301 → api.whatsapp.com/send), zero JS console errors (only unrelated Permissions-Policy: 'bluetooth' warning from WhatsApp's landing page). Regression: existing merchant poster endpoint /api/merchant/panel/qr/poster still returns 200 for fmt=png (with & without caption) and fmt=pdf (spot-check with valid merchant JWT). Expo-web tunnel flow was already fully exercised in iter105 and is not re-run here.

critical.issue: Caption is embedded into the inline <script> block as `const CAP=<json.dumps(caption)>` but Python's json.dumps does NOT escape the sequence '</' — so a caption containing '</script>' (or an attacker-supplied merchant name / caption) will prematurely close the outer <script> tag and inject arbitrary HTML into the page. Reproduced with `caption=<script>alert(1)</script>hi` — the response body contains literal `const CAP="<script>alert(1)</script>hi", TITLE=…` and the browser HTML parser terminates the <script> at the first `</script>`. Because #cap is later populated via innerHTML with HTML-escaping, the *display* is safe, but the *page structure itself* is broken — this is a stored/reflected XSS surface on a public, un-auth'd endpoint that accepts arbitrary caption= query param.
critical.fix: In services/qr_share_page_service.py, replace `json.dumps(caption or "")` (and the same for TITLE / FILE / WA) with a variant that escapes </, <, > for safe inlining inside <script>. Minimal fix: `json.dumps(x).replace('</', '<\\/')` — or use `json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=True).replace('<', '\\u003c').replace('>', '\\u003e').replace('&', '\\u0026')`.

action_items: Fix reflected-XSS / script-breakout in qr_share_page_service.share_page: escape '</' (and ideally <, >, & as \u escapes) inside the CAP / TITLE / FILE / WA JSON literals that are inlined into the <script> block. Endpoint is public (no auth) so this is high-severity.

rca of the issue: share_page() builds a full <script>…const CAP={json.dumps(caption)}…</script> HTML page. Python's json.dumps produces valid JSON, but JSON allows the two-character sequence '</' unchanged. When that JSON literal is inlined inside an HTML <script> element, the HTML parser (per the HTML spec's script-data state) terminates the <script> element at the first '</script' sequence in the raw source — regardless of JSON quoting. Consequence: attacker-controlled caption (public endpoint, no auth) can inject arbitrary HTML after the closing </script>. The runtime HTML-escaping applied by capEl.innerHTML=CAP.replace(...) only protects the *display* text inside #cap; it does not protect the source-level HTML parsing. Mitigation: escape '</' → '<\\/' (and '<!--', '<script') in every json.dumps result inlined into <script>. Two-line fix in qr_share_page_service.py.
